misconceptions.label: Image forms on the mirror surface itself
misconceptions.remedy: Images are located by where reflected rays (or their extensions) intersect, which is generally not at the mirror.

misconceptions.label: Vision works by light travelling from the eye to the object
misconceptions.remedy: Light travels from a source, reflects off the object, and enters the eye.

misconceptions.label: A concave mirror always forms a real image
misconceptions.remedy: Inside the focus, a concave mirror forms a virtual, erect, enlarged image.

misconceptions.label: Focal length equals the radius of curvature
misconceptions.remedy: For a spherical mirror f = R/2.

misconceptions.label: Distances substituted without sign convention
misconceptions.remedy: All distances are measured from the pole; those against the incident light direction are negative.

misconceptions.label: Negative magnification is read as a smaller image
misconceptions.remedy: The sign of m gives orientation (inverted/erect); the modulus gives size.

misconceptions.label: Refraction and reflection are conflated
misconceptions.remedy: Reflection returns light into the same medium; refraction transmits it into a second medium with a change in direction.

misconceptions.label: Light is said to bend away from the normal entering a denser medium
misconceptions.remedy: Entering a denser medium light slows and bends toward the normal.

misconceptions.label: Refractive index is given units
misconceptions.remedy: It is a ratio of two speeds, so it is dimensionless.

misconceptions.label: Light has the same speed in every medium
misconceptions.remedy: c is maximum in vacuum; v = c/n in a medium.

misconceptions.label: A convex lens always magnifies
misconceptions.remedy: Beyond 2F the image is diminished; magnification depends on object position.

misconceptions.label: Lens power computed with focal length in centimetres
misconceptions.remedy: P = 1/f with f in metres, giving dioptres.

misconceptions.label: The eye focuses by moving the lens
misconceptions.remedy: Ciliary muscles change the curvature, and so the focal length, of the eye lens.

misconceptions.label: Myopia corrected with a convex lens
misconceptions.remedy: Myopia needs a diverging (concave) lens; hypermetropia needs a converging (convex) one.

misconceptions.label: The sky is blue because it reflects the sea
misconceptions.remedy: Shorter wavelengths scatter more strongly off atmospheric particles.

misconceptions.label: The prism adds colour to white light
misconceptions.remedy: White light already contains the components; the prism separates them by wavelength-dependent refraction.

misconceptions.label: Current is used up as it passes through a component
misconceptions.remedy: Charge is conserved; energy is transferred, current entering a series element equals current leaving.

misconceptions.label: Current is the same in every parallel branch
misconceptions.remedy: Voltage is common across parallel branches; current divides inversely with resistance.

misconceptions.label: Potential difference divides across parallel branches
misconceptions.remedy: Potential difference is identical across parallel branches; it divides in series.

misconceptions.label: Resistances in parallel are added directly
misconceptions.remedy: In parallel the reciprocals add, so the total is less than the smallest resistance.

misconceptions.label: A thicker wire has greater resistance
misconceptions.remedy: R is inversely proportional to cross-sectional area.

misconceptions.label: Resistivity depends on the length or thickness of the wire
misconceptions.remedy: Resistivity is a material property; resistance depends on geometry.

misconceptions.label: Heat produced is taken as proportional to current
misconceptions.remedy: Joule heating gives H = I squared R t, so heat scales with the square of the current.

misconceptions.label: Power computed as V divided by I
misconceptions.remedy: P = VI.

misconceptions.label: Magnetic field lines are drawn intersecting
misconceptions.remedy: Two directions of the field at one point is impossible, so lines never cross.

misconceptions.label: Field lines start and stop at the poles
misconceptions.remedy: Field lines are closed loops, continuing inside the magnet from south to north.

misconceptions.label: Fleming's left- and right-hand rules are swapped
misconceptions.remedy: Left hand for the force on a current-carrying conductor (motor); right hand for induced current (generator).

misconceptions.label: Induced current requires a battery in the coil
misconceptions.remedy: Relative motion changing the flux is what drives the induced current.

misconceptions.label: The earth wire carries current during normal operation
misconceptions.remedy: It is a safety path to ground, used only on a fault.

misconceptions.label: Nuclear energy classed as renewable
misconceptions.remedy: Uranium is a finite, exhaustible fuel.

misconceptions.label: Solar energy has no environmental cost at any stage
misconceptions.remedy: Generation is clean, but manufacture, land use and disposal carry costs.

misconceptions.label: Stars twinkle because their own brightness fluctuates
misconceptions.remedy: Atmospheric refraction varies continuously along the path, so the apparent position and brightness shift.
